feed.title: NPR Topics: World
feed.subtitle: International news, global reporting and analysis from NPR. Plus dispatches from NPR’s State of the World podcast.

entry.title: U.S. envoys meet with Putin in the Kremlin after Ukraine talks in Abu Dhabi
entry.summary: Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff went to the Kremlin to brief Russian President Vladimir Putin and are scheduled to fly later to Ireland for talks with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy.

entry.title: Indonesia's VP resigns as his eligibility and academic credentials are questioned
entry.summary: Raka is the son of former President Joko Widodo. The Constitutional Court and the Supreme Court ruled last month that the documents that Raka submitted regarding his overseas education didn't meet election requirements.

entry.title: Colom wins Mississippi Senate race. And, White House warns Dems over future probes
entry.summary: After more than a week of counting ballots, Scott Colom has narrowly won the Mississippi Senate seat. And, the White House has sent a letter warning Democrats who plan to investigate the administration.

entry.title: Former Ukrainian foreign minister discusses how to bridge gaps between Ukraine, Russia
entry.summary: NPR's A Martinez asks Ukraine's former Foreign Minister Dmytro Kuleba for his proposals to close gaps in talks between Russia, Ukraine and Europe.

entry.title: Former U.S. Ambassador William Taylor discusses the latest Russia-Ukraine talks
entry.summary: NPR's A Martinez speaks with former U.S. ambassador to Ukraine, William Taylor, about the ongoing peace talks between the U.S., Russia and Ukraine.

entry.title: U.S. officials set to meet with Putin, Zelenskyy following Abu Dhabi peace talks
entry.summary: U.S.-mediated talks in Abu Dhabi have wrapped up with an agreement on a Russia-Ukraine prisoner exchange. U.S. negotiators meet with Vladimir Putin on Thursday and Volodymyr Zelenskyy on Friday.

entry.title: Drought threatens Iraq's marshes, risking one of the oldest ways of life
entry.summary: The unique marshes of southern Iraq are beginning to revive after five years of devastating drought. But challenges remain for one of the world's oldest ways of life.

entry.title: Aid groups call on Israel to allow shelters in Gaza amid a humanitarian emergency
entry.summary: Winter storms have brought flooding and deadly landslides to thousands living in tents in Gaza. Palestinians have no where to go after years of devasting war.

entry.title: An Israeli strike on a Gaza hospital kills 6 people, including a doctor and a child
entry.summary: The victims included a surgeon, and dozens more were injured. Israel said it was targeting a Hamas commander and other militants. The commander was not found among the dead.

entry.title: Greetings from Senegal, where breakdancers are competing in the Youth Olympics
entry.summary: Senegal's breakdancers have been practicing for their country's historic hosting of the Youth Olympic Games this month. It's the first time Africa is hosting an Olympic event.
